journey.name: Speak — pronunciation practice in study
journey.description: The Speak study feature: on a speak-enabled deck, reveal a card back and start pronunciation practice. Actual speech cannot be synthesized in automation, so this journey verifies the permission prompt and the Listening sheet appear and that cancel/retry work, and that a listen producing no answer is reported rather than closing the sheet; the Correct/Wrong outcome is a manual check. Which *language* each engine uses is likewise ear-only — see the Listen step at the end. Requires a signed-in session with at least one due card in a speak-enabled deck (run journeys 01–02 first).

actions.action: Launch the Loopky app and verify the Home screen is shown
Tap the element with resource-id "tab_decks" in the bottom tab bar
Open a deck that was published with the Speak option enabled AND a front/back language pair, and start studying it

Manual check: open a deck published before the language pair existed (or one whose pair is unset) and verify the card back shows neither the Listen nor the Speak button — an undeclared deck must not fall back to the phone's locale
Verify the study card (resource-id: study_card) is shown front-side
Verify "Listen" (resource-id: study_listen) and "Speak" (resource-id: study_speak) are shown on the card FRONT — both sides carry them
Manual check: tap Listen here and verify the prompt is read in the deck's FRONT language, not the back's and not the phone's
Tap the card to reveal the back and verify both buttons are still shown
Tap the element with resource-id "study_speak"
Verify an in-app rationale dialog appears first explaining that Speak listens to your pronunciation, with a Continue action (resource-id: permission_continue)
Tap the element with resource-id "permission_continue" and verify the Android RECORD_AUDIO permission dialog then appears; grant it
Manual check: deny twice so Android stops asking, tap Speak again, and verify a "Microphone is off" dialog offers "Open settings" (resource-id: permission_open_settings) instead of doing nothing
Verify the Listening sheet appears with a microphone indicator (resource-id: speak_mic) and the target word
Manual check: the recognizer listens in the deck's BACK language, not the phone's — on an English-locale device, say the Spanish answer to a Spanish-back deck and verify it is transcribed as Spanish

Manual check (speech not automatable): say the word and verify either the "Perfect!" sheet with Continue (resource-id: speak_continue) or the "Not quite right" sheet with your transcript (resource-id: speak_heard) and Try again (resource-id: speak_retry)

Say nothing at all and wait. Verify the sheet REPORTS the failure (resource-id: speak_failed_title) with a reason and a Try again — it must never close on its own, and must never sit on "Say the word" for good: a sheet that vanishes is indistinguishable from the app having missed the tap
Verify the failure buzzed a Reject (constant=17 in `dumpsys vibrator_manager`), distinct from the ContextClick that opened the microphone — on iOS these are `.error` and a light impact

Tap Try again from that failure sheet and verify it goes straight back to the Listening sheet — a second listen started before the first recognizer is destroyed comes back as "Still listening" instead

Manual check: set the deck to a language with no installed speech model and verify the sheet says "Language not installed" with a Close (resource-id: speak_failed_close) rather than a Try again that would repeat the same failure
Dismiss the Listening sheet and verify the study card is shown again

Tap the Listen button (resource-id: study_listen) on the card back and verify — by ear — that the answer is spoken by a voice for the deck's back language, and the front (before reveal) by the front language's voice. This is the acceptance test; a green build says nothing about which voice was used.
Manual check: set the deck to a language with no installed voice and verify a toast says so rather than the card being read in the wrong accent
